reviews.text: If risk of rain, a reverse form of vampire survivors and summoner wars (the old WCIII frozen throne custom map) had an ugly drunk get together in the closet, this is probably what you get. I mean that in the most positive way. This goes from "WTF am I even doing here?" to "finally, I found the assassin's cloak, now my dodge-army build comes online, you're all ♥♥♥♥♥♥!" real fast. Also, spooky, scary skeletons! And certified banger soundtrack. Skilltrees. But so far, no other trees. But goats. The bad kind. With axes. Which probably explains the "no trees" issues. Oh, and levelling up your creatures gives me a lot of dopamine. Sometimes, when you have different creatures, that aren't too different, they get together and swear, apparently oats are involved... I dunno, I have ADHD and I am not a linguist. TL;DR: Game go BRRRRR, much lights, much gore, no trees, but goats and lots of skeletons. And oats.

Some cool ideas and really nice pixel art on the minions, but way too much grinding and repetition for way too little content. Later levels are simply impossible if you don't grind the meta progression and grinding it takes forever. Re-rolling is too cheap and so way too much time is spent in menus re-rolling rewards, like 50% of gametime. This is extra tedious because there really aren't a whole lot of items. You'll probably have seen 80% of the items in your first run and most are boring %increases to attack/defense/economy. There need to be way more interesting items that change up the runs with cool mechanics/interactions. Lastly, this game needs a detailed damage-done breakdown for individual units/skills/mitigation etc. - Currently it's impossible to really understand why a stat, mechanic or build is good, which is unfortunate because experimentation with oaths/units is the best thing about Skull Horde. I hope they patch this game because there is a lot of potential - In its current form it's a thumbs down from me though. Edit: It's never gonna happen, but here I wish the devs would do: - remove all the %increase stat items (basically anything non-purple?) - let minions provide stat bonuses, i.e. %crit per assassin, %life per Bulwark (or maybe work it the oaths), etc, more/better minions=more stats. - make minion selection more like a deckbuilder: Right now you can buy as many specific minions as you want, you're only limited by gold. Instead there should be a more limited random selection of minions available each run,forcing us to adapt and to make each run different. Minions (of higher ranks) could even be made available as item drops or in the store, offering incentive to explore new combinations - double (or more) the reroll price and cap the free rerolls at 2 or 3

Put them boney dukes up, chug your calcium, and get ready to rumble in the bone zone. Skull Horde is a fantastic horde style game where you get minions to do most if not all of your fighting for you, but you can still find skills along the way so that you alone become the chosen one. The various characters all have their own unique styles of play where I inevitably finished a run focusing heavily on crits no matter what because im a basic bish of a skull. It feels great when I finally manage to get a few levels in and start building a massive horde especially with the actual horde summons that just fill my screen til my pc starts screaming from the overload. Skull Horde is really well balanced, but it is really rough to win even the easiest of levels until you actually get some levels in because the initial phase is insanely weak. Once you start getting strong however then no matter what you build you will end up bone dozing your way through everything really quickly, Skull Horde is so far one of my favorite games to come out this year and that is not fully due to my bias towards horde game, but because this is a genuinely fun game and I was supposed to finish up other games before diving too deep here. No matter flesh is temporary and bone is eternal, fo sho pick this game up for yerself.

The skill tree upgrades don’t feel like they have any effect on the game and even though I am trying to unlock new characters the RNG just does not give me what I need. I am going to give the game a couple more hours to see if I finally do manage to unlock a new character or level but after that I’m just gonna have to add it to the pile of failed roguelikes. [b]Update:[/b] I played for two more hours and nothing really changed. I did unlock a new character but all it really did was start the same grind again, which still hasn’t become fun.

7/10——瑕不掩瑜的佳作，策略宽松，偏爽游，适合打发时间 加分项： - 核心体验OK：合理配置兵种真的能成群，不同主角玩法上有差别，但都还是比较符合想象中带着一大群骷髅小弟杀杀杀的那种感觉。 - 优秀的美术设计：敌人都是红色系（血肉），我方都是黑绿色系，区分度不错。扫描线可开关，我感觉不太正宗而且看着有点头晕，所以我是关掉的。建议开发者可以多看一下老的恶魔城拍屏，扫描线会让像素有色散，不是这样公整的像素方块。不过不追求这种质感的话，单从像素美术的角度也是一流的了。 - 宽松的策略设计，不按头限制玩法：局内可以花钱Ban掉遗物和兵种，让其不再出现在随机池中。遗物数值给得还算全面，可以搓成很极端的数值（喜欢我万甲盾哥，0.1s复活鼠王，百爆狙击手吗？）。羁绊凑成后卖掉也生效，有规划后不算太难凑。但部分遗物有数量上限，导致部分属性比较难获得（例如定值暴击闪避、定值减复活CD、主角技能减CD），要爽还是要一定规划的。当然规划好了后是能逆克制打关卡的。你甚至可以调整水温上升速度和敌人基础数值，想爽想坐牢都随意。 扣分项： - 整体重复度比较高：下层后有哪些东西都直接在地图上了，没有什么突发事件。怪刷完后也是慢慢产生的，每层压力最大、惊喜最多的时候是下层开始探索的时候，后续发育期，每张地图上没什么东西、敌人也给不了压力，就比较无聊了。扩张到不同局之间，随机要素可以roll可以ban的代价就是一个策略吃到死，局与局的重复度也比较高。 - 引导不全：百科全书里没有对属性的解释，我至今不知道护甲是定值减伤还是除法公式减伤还是衰减公式减伤，不知道铲子的增加可破坏物掉率是怎么个增加法，不知道运气的作用原理，以至于很多时候我无法判断属性价值。Buff都有了给属性加个悬停解释，或者是在百科里加一页也可以。 - 容易卡死：我一直在玩剧团的鼠王亡语流，偶尔会有场上大概两三百个衍生物鼠鼠的时候游戏卡死，无法操作只能大退。大退后是从这层开始重开的，但我刷经验的话，最后一层可能刷一个多小时，这种时候重开就很破坏体验了。

It's got a fun premise and core gameplay, but the way the game adds difficulty isn't all that fun. It just adds more enemies with faster respawns and more debuffs against the player. I wouldn't mind it as much if the game gave you more rewarding progression. The buffs you get from perks top out at around 10%, which for me took about 3 hours for one full tree. I think this game has potential, but they need to work on balancing and improving upon the skill trees and perks. I wish steam had a "neutral" rating, but I guess I'll have to give it a thumbs down for now.

[b]RECOMMENDED[/b] (even at full price) Starts very slowly and I almost gave up on the idea this could be fun after the first hour or so. But I came back to it, and glad I did! Once you get a few upgrades and really lean into the strengths/weaknesses of each of the necromancers, it really is a blast to dive into for a 20-30m run or two. You can do runs much quicker, I just like taking my time and unleashing the power fantasy :) More maps and biomes would be a good addition, but there's enough there right now to easily get 40+ hours out of it, and much more with Endless. The pixel art is lovely, the audio fx are crunchy and satisfiying, and the soundtrack is absolutely fantastic. Real bangers. When starting out, I recommend getting inspiration from the Achievements tab in the game menu and pinning a few each run, that's what really opened up the game for me. It also helped me learn (and bother to learn) how the different Champions could work with each other. i.e. what different "builds" looked like and played like. Before I started looking in there I was really stumped how the run-to-run variation was meant to happen, given it's a rogue-like. The meta-unlocks happen quite slowly so without the build experimentation nudges from the above, I would have just done every run exactly the same and got bored grinding very quickly. Who knew an All Rats Run would be so hilariously OP... I think I'm probably not alone in that experience as the completion rates of achievements is very low. Well worth the price, as it turns out!

The game is promising, but it lacks the depth I would expect from a roguelite. The biggest issue is that interesting builds are almost entirely locked behind RNG. No matter what strategy you have in mind, whether you can play it depends on luck rather than your decisions. As a result, most runs end up feeling very similar. Your "build" isn't something you create through meaningful choices; it's simply whatever the game happens to offer you. I think many of the negative reviews here could have been avoided with a few design changes. For example, limiting the number of upgrades you can take would make each choice more meaningful, or adding a less punishing banish system would give players more control over their builds. The progression also feels unnecessarily grindy. After 5.5 hours of gameplay, I had barely made progress toward fully upgrading a single character. For a game of this size, especially one that is purely single-player, that amount of grinding feels excessive and doesn't add much to the experience.
